items.question: Who is the supreme partless eternal being free from disease and stainless?
premises: Supreme partless eternal being is described.
Freedom from disease and stainlessness are attributed.
The being is identified as he.
items.inference: The supreme being is partless, eternal, and stainless.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: Who is the more supreme soul called haṃsa and power-individual?
premises: The soul is called more supreme.
The soul is identified as haṃsa.
items.inference: The haṃsa soul is the more supreme power-individual.
uncertainties: Comparative force of parataro is approximate.
items.plain_english: He is the soul, the more supreme haṃsa, a power-individual.

items.question: Where is the wind-filled air situated among all beings?
premises: It is situated in all beings.
items.inference: The wind-filled air is situated in all beings.
uncertainties: Neuter agreement of saṃsthitam is approximate.
items.plain_english: The wind-filled air is situated in all beings.

items.question: Upon merely leaving the body, is the jīva called supreme Śiva?
items.inference: The jīva becomes supreme Śiva upon bodily departure.
uncertainties: paraṃ may be adjectival rather than predicative
items.plain_english: He, upon merely leaving the body, is called supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is the teaching heard abiding in the ear through tradition?
premises: the teaching abides in the ear
it is heard by the goddess
items.inference: The tradition is heard as something abiding in the ear.
uncertainties: whether karṇa+sthaṃ modifies the teaching or the hearer
items.plain_english: Abiding in the ear, it is heard, O goddess, come down through tradition.

premises: it suffices for the fair-faced one

items.plain_english: By this mere knowledge heard, O fair-faced one.
